Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 48
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Oceania
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Roofer
  trauma_type: Sexual assault
  pcl5: 47

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Media / News: Related news, Auditory/Mechanical: Motorcycle noise, Olfactory (Alcohol): Alcohol smell
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Physical Stress: Situations that put my body under stress, Restrict Eating: control eating strictly to feel in control, Busyness: I work hard at keeping busy with other things
  Memory: More Real Than Normal: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things, Emotion Without Image: Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory, Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief

Vignette:
John, a 48-year-old married man from Oceania, works as a roofer and has experienced significant psychological distress following a traumatic sexual assault. His journey through this trauma began several months ago when he was assaulted by an acquaintance at a local bar after having a few drinks. The event itself remains vividly etched in his mind — the dim lighting of the bar, the smell of alcohol permeating the air, and the sudden intrusion into his personal space that culminated in his assault. Since then, John has found himself acutely sensitive to certain triggers that remind him of this night. The sound of motorcycles, which he associates with the vehicle used by his assailant, often sends jolts of anxiety through him. Similarly, any news related to sexual assaults reported on television or heard about in conversations can plunge him into a state of distress. John’s memories of the assault feel more real and vivid than other memories. Sometimes, without any clear image surfacing, he experiences the full emotional intensity of that night — feelings of shame, fear, and grief flood his consciousness. These intense emotions often lead to periods where John feels overwhelmed by sorrow, leaving him feeling isolated from those around him. To cope with these overwhelming feelings, John has developed several maladaptive strategies. One of the most notable is his strict control over eating, which gives him a sense of predictability and order in an otherwise chaotic mental landscape. He also avoids situations that put his body under stress, like strenuous physical activity, despite it being a core part of his job as a roofer. This has led to conflicts at work, where he finds himself unable to perform some tasks due to his fear of triggering the intense distress associated with physical exertion. To further manage his anxiety, John keeps himself busy with other activities and responsibilities, often working longer hours or taking on extra projects. While this busyness provides a temporary distraction from his intrusive thoughts and memories, it has strained his relationship with his wife. She notices that he is increasingly distant and less available to engage in their usual family life. John’s avoidance behaviors have started to take a toll not only on his work but also on his personal relationships. His wife often expresses concern about his increasing isolation and the changes she observes in him, yet John finds it hard to open up and share what he is experiencing. The fear of being vulnerable again and the persistent feeling that something bad could happen if he lets his guard down have made him guarded and emotionally withdrawn. It was a particularly distressing encounter at work — where a colleague’s motorcycle backfired, sending John into an intense panic attack in front of everyone — that finally pushed him to seek help. The overwhelming grief and the realization that his coping mechanisms are no longer sustainable have left him feeling both desperate for relief and hopeful that therapy might provide some solace. In seeking help, John is most afraid of reliving the trauma through recounting it in therapy sessions. However, he also harbors a glimmer of hope that understanding and addressing these memories could alleviate his current distress and allow him to reclaim his life without the constant fear and avoidance that have become so prevalent.
